source: Amsterdam street panoramas (data.amsterdam.nl, CC BY 4.0), newest facing capture per pand (scripts/retail-ground/front-photos.ts --hosts --newest); read by fresh Claude Opus agents, 90 fronts each
prompt:
You read Amsterdam shopfronts from street panoramas to correct OpenStreetMap. Read the claims file named below: each entry has an id, an image path (a perspective cut from a street panorama aimed at the ground storey where OSM puts the business; the aim point is the middle of the image), the OSM claim (name and tags) and the photo date. Open each image with the Read tool, one by one. Open nothing else.

For each entry, judge the ground-floor unit at or nearest the middle of the image:
- "match": the claimed business, or one of the claimed kind, is there (a readable sign agrees, or the kind is clear and nothing contradicts it)
- "other": a different business occupies the middle unit. Give its OSM tag (one of shop=<value> or amenity=<value>, e.g. shop=clothes, shop=gift, amenity=cafe, amenity=restaurant, amenity=bar, amenity=fast_food, shop=bakery, shop=hairdresser, shop=tattoo, shop=mobile_phone, shop=bicycle, amenity=brothel ...) and the name on its sign if readable
- "noShop": the middle ground floor has no shopfront: a house, office entrance, church, blank wall
- "vacant": an empty, papered-over or under-renovation shopfront
- "unreadable": a shopfront is clearly there, but what it sells cannot be told
- "occluded": the ground floor cannot be seen (vehicle, tree, crowd, scaffold, wrong wall, too far)
Give "conf" from 0 to 1: how sure you are of the verdict (and, for "other", of the tag). Be strict: 0.9+ only when a sign or the window plainly shows it.

Write JSON to the output path named below as {"<id>": {"v": "...", "tag": "<only for other>", "name": "<sign text if read, else empty>", "conf": 0.0}, ...} covering every id. Reply with counts per verdict only.
